correctness.rationale: Homogeneity fixes the type once the named adjacency vector is fixed; any such vector is realized by finite extension since the old graph is triangle-free. With two new adjacent vertices the only possible K4 uses both new vertices and an old edge inside their common neighborhood, including when the two types are equal. Thus the matrix is the Boolean meet matrix of the independence indicator. Its zeta congruence is integral and invertible, with diagonal h(U)=(-1)^|U| I_{G[U]}(-1). Independent enumeration used a lexicographic canonical code over degree-ordered relabelings (no heuristic isomorphism filter) and exact alternating subset sums. Every admissible graph occurs by deleting its last vertex and extending by an independent neighborhood. The enumeration recovers the order-eight frequencies 1,35,253,111,9,1 for values −2,−1,0,1,2,3; the sole 3 is canonically Q3. All smaller orders, including the empty graph with sum 1, have no nonzero odd-prime-divisible value, so all proper induced subgraphs at order eight are harmless as well. Independent Boolean subtraction gives 138 zeros, 105 units, twelve absolute twos and one three, with 60 positive and 58 negative entries. Combining one twosummand with the threesummand gives 106 Smith units, eleven factors 2 and one factor 6, with 138 zeros; the reported cokernel and ranks follow.
residual_risks: The finite threshold does not classify larger graphs, bases containing triangles, or other forbidden cliques.

value.rationale: The finite cutoff addresses the least size at which characteristics other than 2 can change the rank of the adjacent-type matrix. It separates a natural extremizer from all smaller and equal-order competitors rather than reporting a handpicked cube evaluation. The full field-rank comparison and unique Smith factor divisible by 3 give a reusable explicit obstruction for work on logical type matrices and induced independence sums.
residual_risks: No uniform bound or structural classification at larger orders is implied.
